title: 7 Best Frontend Options for Django in 2026
summary: Seven ways to put a frontend on a Django backend, from server-rendered templates to SPAs and no-code internal tools.
body_markdown:
Django ships with templates and an admin, which is enough for many projects. The question of which frontend to use usually comes up in two places: the product UI your customers see, and the internal tools your team uses to run the business. The right answer is often different for each.


Below are seven frontend options for Django, with the point where each one stops. For database clients, see the[best Django GUI tools](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/best-django-gui-tools/) .

## Internal frontends


### 1. Jet Admin


Jet Admin connects to the database behind Django (Postgres, MySQL and others) or to your Django REST API, and builds internal tools: record pages, forms, approval steps and dashboards. You describe the app and Jet generates it, then refine it visually or in code. There is no second copy of the data.


Operations, support and finance teams get their own logins and only what their role allows, without developers building every screen. Granular permissions, SSO and audit logs are on the Business plan and above; unlimited users are on every plan, including Free.


**Where it stops:** it is not for your customer-facing product UI.


### 2. Django admin themes


Themes such as Unfold, Jazzmin and Grappelli restyle the built-in admin with little code.


**Where it stops:** the admin's model-by-model structure stays; custom workflows still need code.


### 3. Retool


Retool connects to the Django database or API, and developers build internal tools with components and JavaScript.


**Where it stops:** developer-built, with per-user pricing.


## Product frontends


### 4. Django templates with htmx


Server-rendered templates with htmx add interactivity without a JavaScript build step or a separate API.


**Where it stops:** highly interactive, app-like screens get awkward.


### 5. React


React with Django REST Framework or Django Ninja is the most common split-stack setup.


**Where it stops:** two codebases, an API layer and auth handling to maintain.


### 6. Vue


Vue works as a full SPA or as components dropped into Django templates.


**Where it stops:** the same API and build overhead as React once it grows.


### 7. Next.js


Next.js adds server rendering and routing on top of React, with Django as the API.


**Where it stops:** another server to host and more moving parts.


## Which to use


- **Your team needs internal tools on Django data without developer time:** Jet Admin.
- **You want the built-in admin to look better:** an admin theme.
- **Product UI with a small team:** templates with htmx.
- **Complex, app-like product UI:** React, Vue or Next.js with an API.
- **Developers will build internal tools:** Retool.


## Frequently asked questions


### Do I need Django REST Framework for a frontend?


Only for a separate JavaScript frontend. Templates, htmx and tools that connect to the database directly do not need it.


### Should internal tools use the same frontend as the product?


Usually not. Internal tools change often and need permissions more than polish, so building them in the product stack uses expensive developer time.
